duties.duty: ED26-P15-CH-product-measures-C013 (partial): The full treatment promised by the declared status proved=annex:p15.absolute-iterated-series is not supplied. The series half of the proof connects the corollary's sums to Fubini's integrals only through two bare assertions. The first is 'The assumed sum is the first iterated absolute integral, because integration with respect to kappa is summation' (handbook/annex/p15/product-measures.tex 514-515). The second is 'counting-measure integration of that integrable section equals the sum' (519-521). Neither identity is derived in this proof or established anywhere on the route: the integral against counting measure on N+ of a nonnegative g equals the sum of g(n), and the signed version holds for an absolutely summable section. The closest result, thm:p15-expectation-law-integral (handbook/parts/p15/integration-expectation.tex 324-348), gives the sum formula only for countable atomic probability spaces. Three identifications are therefore unwritten: the hypothesis sum of the integrals of |f_n| with Fubini's premise, H with the section absolute integral (516-518), and S with Fubini's second section-integral function (522-523). All other parts of C013 (the Tonelli criterion at 499-504, product measurability of F, the absolute-convergence bound, integrability of each f_n) are written.
duties.note: The two bare assertions the duty quotes are no longer in the file. The nonnegative counting identity (integral of g >= 0 against counting measure on N+ equals the sum of g(k), infinite values included) is derived at annex 514-533 and the signed version for absolutely summable real g at 534-550. The three identifications are written: the hypothesis sum with the first iterated absolute integral and hence the Fubini premise (570-580), H with the second absolute section integral H_2 and N with N_2 (582-595), and S with Fubini's second signed section-integral function I_2F at every point (597-606); the exchange follows at 608-626. The other parts the duty lists as written (criterion 499-504, product measurability of F 552-559, absolute-convergence bound 613-618, integrability of each f_n 609-612) remain present.
